text:
Maria: Heads-up — saw a spike in GPU pod restarts during spot reclaims this morning in us-west-2. Several inference pods ended up pending for 6+ minutes.
Jon: Noted. Any specific node groups or instance-types? :thinking_face:
Maria: Mostly mixed-pool: g4dn.xlarge spot + p3-standard reserved fallback. The autoscaler moved things around but drains looked slow.
Kevin: Do we still use node.kubernetes.io/instance-lifecycle=spot NoSchedule taint on the spot group?
Maria: Yes. But many of our inference pods have tolerations so they get scheduled on spot, which is fine until reclaim.
Sarah: What was the reclaim signal? AWS termination notice? infra-bot, did it log anything? :eyes:
infra-bot: aws-tn-handler detected termination for i-0bcd1234 at 2026-04-06T09:12:05Z. Node cordon at 09:12:07, drain started at 09:12:12.
Jon: Drain start 5s after cordon is fine, but what about graceful terminationGracePeriodSeconds on pods? Inference pods default to 30s.
Maria: Exactly — the problem is large batching + KV cache flushs take ~90s. PreStop isn't configured to persist state.
Kevin: We should add a preStop hook for inference containers to checkpoint KV cache and async-ack requests. Example snippet we could apply:

```
lifecycle:
  preStop:
    exec:
      command: ["/bin/sh", "-c", "./save_kv_cache.sh && sleep 5"]
```

Maria: That helps but still depends on node termination window. AWS spot notice gives 120s, GCP preemptible gives 30s — need different handling per cloud.
Sarah: For short notice clouds we must aggressively prioritize shifting traffic away from spot nodes earlier. Maybe use taint with PreferNoSchedule followed by NoSchedule on notice?
Jon: Idea: On termination notice, infra handler adds label spot-terminating=true, then a K8s controller patches pods to decrease traffic weight or mark readiness false. We already have a readiness-probe-override sidecar for rollout; could reuse it.
Kevin: Also check cluster-autoscaler behavior: it may not scale up fast enough when many spot nodes drop. We should pre-warm fallback reserved nodes or keep a small buffer pool of on-demand GPUs.
Maria: Proposed policy: maintain 10% reserved GPU capacity per region for critical inference. Use mixed pools with taints + podPriority for non-critical batch jobs.
Sarah: For scheduling, use nodeAffinity for batch jobs to prefer spot nodes. Inference core pods get strict toleration + higher priority and avoid spot when reserved available.
Jon: Config suggestions for CA: set --scale-down-unneeded-time to 5m -> maybe too aggressive. For spot churn, increase to 10m and set expander to least-waste.
autoscaler-bot: cluster-autoscaler event: scaled up nodegroup gpu-reserved-usw2 by 2 at 2026-04-06T09:13:40Z.
Maria: PDBs are in place but we should lower maxUnavailable for stateful workloads. Also add an alert: spot-reclaim-rate > 5% over 15m -> page.
Kevin: We also need faster drains. Use `kubectl drain --delete-local-data --grace-period=60 --ignore-daemonsets` via handler instead of controller default.
Sarah: Worth testing lifecycle hook that sets `node.kubernetes.io/terminating=true` then uses a pre-drain hook to set readiness false on critical pods so they stop taking new requests immediately.
Jon: Alternative: use Karpenter for opportunistic capacity and node-lifecycle webhooks; it has faster replacement behavior but more complexity.
Maria: Ops runbook draft:
- On spot termination notice: cordon -> set terminating label -> call readiness sidecar -> preStop checkpoint -> drain with 60s grace -> if not done, force-evict.
- If >3 nodes reclaimed in 10m, spin up reserved fallback pool automatically.

Kevin: Can we add a small script for the handler to annotate pods with `redwood/skip-drain=false` for batch to allow immediate eviction? Quick patchable.
Sarah: I'll prototype the readiness sidecar change and the handler labeling today.
Jon: I'll adjust CA flags in staging: --scale-down-unneeded-time=10m, --max-node-provision-time=15m, set expander=least-waste.
infra-bot: Created ticket INFRA-1427: Add preStop checkpoint + termination labeling + CA tuning (https://redwood.atlassian.net/browse/INFRA-1427)
Maria: Thanks. After prototyping, let's run a controlled reclaim test in staging with synthetic spot interruptions.
Kevin: Agreed — will schedule test tomorrow 09:00 PT. Will measure pod restart time, request latency spikes, and cost delta.
Sarah: FYI: I pushed a small toleration strictness change to the canary cluster; logs are quiet so far.
Maria: Perfect. If anyone wants to pair on the sidecar code, ping me. :thumbsup:
Jon: Pinged. I'll help with CA tuning and the test harness.
Kevin: I'll prepare the fallback reserved pool template and IAM hooks.
infra-bot: Reminder: runbook for node termination is in internal docs: https://redwood.internal/runbooks/node-termination
Maria: Closing the loop — we'll reconvene after the staging run with metrics and a rollback plan.
Sarah: Thanks everyone.
